_comment: What the Figma variables currently say, mirrored into git. Figma's Variables REST API is Enterprise-only, so nothing running locally can fetch this on a Professional plan — refreshing this file is a Claude/MCP job, not a script. app/__tests__/figma-contract.test.ts fails when it stops matching the CSS cascade below, so a token changed in Figma and never applied in code shows up as a red test instead of as a colour nobody notices is wrong.

_cascade.note: The effective value of a token is app/app/_generated/tokens.css (generated from omega-docs) with app/app/styles/tokens.css layered on top. Two tokens below are the override layer's values, not the generated ones — that is deliberate, the override is what actually renders.

_notModelled.note: These exist in CSS but are not Figma variables, because Figma has no equivalent primitive. Do not add them as variables — they will only drift.

figmaResolved._comment: Figma variables cannot hold color-mix() or var() references, so computed tokens are stored resolved. If the inputs change in CSS these must be recomputed by hand — the test cannot catch that for you.
figmaResolved.dark.panel-fill: #101012 — resolves color-mix(in oklab, var(--muted) 45%, var(--card)); the .panel substrate in app/app/styles/materials.css

landing._comment: Landing-only literals that are hardcoded in the component today rather than tokenised. Modelled in Figma as color/landing/hero-top so they are editable; applying a change means editing the inline style in landing-hero.tsx.
